lawyer:
Golam Mohammad Chowdhury, Deputy Attorney- General with Giasuddin Mithu, Assistant Attorney- General ----- For the State. 
Shakhawat Hossain, State Defence Lawyer ----- For the Condemned Prisoner.
parties:
Rafiqul Islam Mollah (Md) ------ Condemned Prisoner 
vs 
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Sikder Maqbul Huq J: This death reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is for confirmation of death sentence inflicted upon the condemned accused Rafiqul Islam Mollah for the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code in Sessions Case No. 32 of 1997 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Gopalganj. 

 2. Prosecution case, stated briefly, is that SaIma Begum, daughter of Pachu Sharif of village Choto Bahirbap PS Kashiani District Gopalganj was given in marriage with sole accused Md Rafiqul Islam Mollah of village Sutfa, PS and District- Gopalganj. About 4 months before the date of occurrence, Salma was brought to the house of her husband and she began living there with him. On 9-2-1994, Pachu Sharif received information through PW 2 Eku Mollah that his daughter had died in the house of his son-in-law in the night following 8-2-1994. Pachu Sharif then went there and saw the dead body of his daughter lying on the floor of the verandah of the dwelling house of the accused. He then went to Gopalganj Police Station and made statement to the above effect whereupon UD Case No.7 of 1994 dated 10-2-1994 was started by the charge officer of the Thana and he himself took up inquiry into the case, went to the place of occurrence, prepared inquest on the dead body of victim Salma and sent the same to Gopalgonj morgue for post-mortem examination. Doctor holding post-mortem examination gave opinion that the death of the victim was due to shock as a result of the injuries found on her person which were ante mortem and homicidal in nature. On receipt of the post-mortem report the aforesaid charge officer, being PW 1 Md Nurul Amin, lodged the FIR on 7-3-1994 mentioning the above facts and entrusted PW 11 SI Md Majibur Rahman with investigation. PW 11 investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet against Md Rafiqul Islam Mollah, husband of victim Salma Begum. 

 3. The accused absconded after the occurrence and the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalganj, framed charge against him in his absence for the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code and the case was subsequently tried by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Gopalganj. 

 5. Prosecution examined 10 witnesses in support of its case and also tendered one witness for cross-examination by the defence. 

 7. The defence case, as it appears from the trend of cross-examination, is that the accused was not at home in the night of occurrence and that the accused was watching television elsewhere in the night of occurrence and it is also alternatively suggested that the accused was a rickshaw puller in Dhaka and he was there at the relevant time. 

 8. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, on consideration of the evidence of the witnesses and attending facts and circumstances of the case, found that the accused had committed murder of his wife and passed the impugned order of conviction and sentence and made this reference for confirmation of death sentence by its Memo No. 111/Crl/Addl. dated the 24th day of February, 2003. 

 11. Mr Giasuddin Mithu, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, submits that it has been proved by the evidence of the witnesses that the accused and the victim were in the same house at the time of occurrence and he absconded immediately after commission of murder of his wife and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, considering the pros and cons of the case, has come to a finding that the accused committed murder of his wife. It is further submitted that ascendance of the accused from the date of occurrence also indicates his complicity in the murder of his wife. It is further submitted that the victim was in the custody of the accused at the relevant time and the accused husband is under legal obligation to give an explanation as to how his wife met with her death in his house. In support of his contention the learned Assistant Attorney-General has referred to the decision in the case of Giasuddin vs State, reported in 55 DLR 328; in the case of Shah Alam and others vs State, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 31; in the case of State vs Md Shafiqul Islam @ Rafiq and another, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 92. 

 12. Mr Shakhawat Hossain, the learned State Defence Lawyer appearing for the condemned accused, on the other hand, submits that there is no eye-witness of the occurrence and, as such, the trial Court ought to have acquitted the accused. It is further submitted that there is no evidence on record that the accused had any intention to kill his wife or that the murder is a preplanned one or that the accused dealt any blow on the victim and, as such, the case does not come within the mischief of section 302 of the Penal Code. The learned State Defence Lawyer further submits that even if this Court finds the sole accused guilty, the order of conviction and sentence should be altered to one under section 304 Part II of the Penal Code, and in support of his contention, he has referred to the decision in the case of Bandez Ali @ Md Bandez Ali vs State, reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 5, wherein it has been held that culpable homicide is not murder if it is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel and without the offender having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner. He also refers to the decision in the case of State vs Abul Howlader, reported in 48 DLR 257 which case does not appear to have any bearing in the case before us. The learned State Defence Lawyer also referred to the decision in the case of Arzan @ 1man Ali vs State, reported in 48 DLR 287 also having no relevance in the case before us. 

 (2) 	Whether the case comes within the mischief of section 304 Part II of the Penal Code. 

 14. Let us now consider the evidence of the witnesses examined in the case. 

 PW 1 SI Md Nurul Amin was attached to Gopalganj Police Station on 10-2-1994 as charge officer of the Thana. He started UD Case No.7 of 1994 on the verbal statement of Pachu Sharif, father of the victim Salma Begum, visited the place of occurrence, held inquest on the dead body of the victim in presence of the witnesses and sent the same to Gopalganj morgue through PW 5 constable Mir Abdul Mannan Molla and another constable Mozammel Huq (not examined) and on receipt of the post mortem report lodged first information report with Officer-in-Charge, Gopalganj Police Station to the effect that accused Mr Rafiqul Islam Mollah had killed his wife in the night following 8- 2-1994 and then absconded. He proves the first information report Exhibit 1 and his signature Exhibit 1/1 therein. He also proves the sharee Material Exhibit I arid the petticoat Material Exhibit II, Blouse Material Exhibit III and Churi material Exhibit IV. During cross-examination, he denies the defence suggestion that the accused was not at home in the night of occurrence on 8-2-1994 or that the accused knows nothing regarding the death of his wife. He further denies the defence suggestion to have submitted charge-sheet in the case on being gained over by the father of the victim. 

 16. During cross-examination, this witness says that he went to the place of occurrence on hearing hue and cry and heard of the death of the victim from PW 9 Jamirman Nessa. He denies the defence suggestion not to have stated to the investigating officer that the accused left his homestead on 9-2-94, PW 3 Md Abdul Hye Sheikh also hails from the same village with the accused. He also went to the place of occurrence after hearing the news of the death of the victim from PW 9, his next-door neighbour and saw the dead body of the victim lying in the veranda of the accused. He further says that in his presence Rafiqul, on query of PW 9 Jamiyon, expressed that the victim went to bathroom twice in the night and she died in the morning and then accused Rafiqul went towards the south on foot. This witness also denied the defence suggestion that accused was not at his house in the morning on the aforesaid date or that the victim had quarrel with the accused or that the victim died in the absence of the accused or that he has deposed falsely In this case. 

 23. During cross-examination, this witness says that his homestead is at a distance of 100 yards from the homestead of the accused and in his presence the accused never asked Salma to bring money from her father. He further says that he does not know whether the accused was in his house in the night of occurrence. He denies the defence suggestion that he will be able to enjoy the property of the accused in case of his sentence of death or imprisonment. 

 27. The aforesaid statements of PW 9 could not be shaken during cross-examination. She denies the defence suggestion that she did not go to the house of accused Rafique on the aforesaid morning or that the accused did not tell her anything as stated by her. It has not been suggested to this witness that she has any enmity with the accused or that she has any reason to depose falsely in the case and there appears no reason for this witness to falsely implicate the accused in this case. 

 28. PW 10 Md Kabir Hossain is also a neighbour of the accused. He also went to the place of occurrence after hearing of the death of the victim and saw the dead body. He further says that he also saw the accused at the house when he went there and denies the defence suggestion that the accused was not at home in the morning on 9-2-1994. This suggestion on behalf of the accused lends support to the prosecution case that the accused in the morning on 9-2-94 left his homestead after commission of murder of his wife. This witness also emphatically denies to have falsely implicated the accused in this case and no enmity with the accused could be suggested for his deposing falsely in this case. 

 29. PW 11 SI Md Mojibur Rahman, as mentioned earlier, investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet against the sole accused. He proves the first information report form Exhibit 2 and his signatures Exhibit 2/1 and 2/2 therein. He also proves the sketch Exhibit 3 prepared by him and his signature Exhibit 3/1 therein and also proves the index Exhibit 4 and his signature Exhibit 4/1 therein. 

 30. During cross-examination, this witness denies the defence suggestion that Rafique went to another homestead in the night of occurrence for watching television or that he was not at his house in the night or that the accused does not know anything about the death of his wife. Nothing in support of the defence case could be elicited from this witness during cross-examination. 

 31. No other witness has been examined in this case. 

 32. There is no dispute about the fact that victim Salma Begum was daughter of Pachu Sharif of village Choto Bahirbap, PS Kashiany, District-Gopalganj and she was given in marriage with Rafiqul Islam of village Chotfa within PS and District Gopalganj. There is also no dispute about the fact that the victim was living in the house of the accused from before the date of occurrence. The witnesses saw the dead body of the victim early in the morning on 9-2-94 lying in the verandah of the condemned accused and their evidence in this regard has not been challenged by the defence. PW 1 who held inquest, found injuries on the dead body of the victim and sent the salt for post-mortem examination. PW 6, the doctor holding post mortem examination, found several injuries on the dead body of the victim and on dissection found clotted blood inside the brain and death was caused by above injuries which were ante mortem and homicidal in nature. There is no defence contention that PW 1 who visited the place of occurrence did not find injury on the person of the victim and it is also not challenged that the death of the victim was due to the injuries found by PW 6. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, we find that the victim was done to death in the night of occurrence on 8-2-94. 

 33. Now, the question is, whether the condemned accused Rafiqul Islam committed murder of his wife Salma Begum. We find from the evidence of PWs 2, 3, 9 and 10 that accused Rafique was present in his house early in the morning on the date of occurrence. The accused himself invited PW 9 to go to his house and see his wife and PW 9 then went to his house and saw the victim dead. PW 10 is maternal uncle of the accused. He also saw the accused present in 'his house and also saw the dead body of the victim. He also emphatically denies the defence suggestion that the accused was not in his house at that time. It is also apparent from the evidence of the witnesses that the accused absconded immediately after the occurrence and he is still in abscondence. In this connection, it is argued by the learned Assistant Attorney-General that it has been held in the case of Giasuddin vs State, reported in 55 DLR 328 that as the wife at the relevant time of occurrence was at her husband's house and was subsequently, found dead an obligation is cast upon the defence to account for the circumstance leading to the death of the deceased failing which the husband will be responsible for the death of the deceased. In the instant case no explanation whatsoever could be offered on behalf of the accused as to how the victim met with 'her death in the husband's house. This lends support to the contention of the learned Assistant Attorney-General. It has been held in the case of Mobarak Hossain vs State, reported in 33 DLR 274 that absconding immediately after the murder and remaining in hiding for a long time are relevant facts that the accused was concerned in the murder. Abscondence of the condemned accused immediately after the murder of his wife is a circumstance indicating that he was concerned with the murder of his wife. It has been held in the case of Al-Amin and 5 others vs State, reported in 51 DLR 154, that long abscondence and non-submission to the process of the court speaks volumes against the accused persons and clearly suggest their involvement in the crime. Abscondence of the accused persons furnishes corroboration of the prosecution case and evidence. The reference cited by the learned Advocate for the condemned accused has no relevance for the purpose of arriving at a decision in the case before us. 

 34. The accused was under obligation to offer an explanation regarding death of his wife in his own house but he, instead of offering any such explanation and even making any arrangement for her burial, etc. absconded on the date of occurrence immediately after it took place on 9-2-94 and he is still absconding. We also find materials on record that he used to live an idle life and used to depend on the earning of his wife. It further appears from the record that he used to put pressure on the victim to bring money from her father. Taking into consideration the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and having regard to other materials on record, we find nothing to disagree with the learned Additional Sessions Judge that it was the accused and accused alone who committed murder of his wife in the night following 8-2-94 or in the early hours of 9-2-1994. 

 35. Regarding the submission of the learned State Defence Lawyer that the case comes within the mischief of section 304 Part II of the Penal Code, we are unable to agree with him in view of the fact that there is no allegation of any grave or sudden provocation. In the instant case, there is no defence contention or any material on record to the effect that the accused killed the victim on any provocation whatsoever not to speak of sudden or grave provocation. Thus we are unable to bring the case under section 304 of the Penal Code. 

 36. Now, the question remains, whether the learned Additional Sessions Judge was legally justified in inflicting the sentence of death instead of sentence of imprisonment for life on the accused. The fact of the case does not show that the accused used any heavy or sharp cutting or lethal weapon or even acted with cruelty in committing murder of the victim. There is also nothing on record that the murder was preplanned and cold-blooded. In such view of the matter we hold that it will meet the ends of justice if the sentence of death inflicted upon the condemned accused is reduced to imprisonment for life.
